page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head top left, page number top right. Marginal notes in the right margin beside the second and third paragraphs. Catchword and signature at the foot.

main_text.p: oriente, sinistram uero in occasu. Ex quibus non difficile est colligere, quænam pars cœli anterior, quæue posterior. Ac dextram quidem partem recte in cœlo constitui ad orientem, uel ex eo constare potest, quòd dextrum merito appellatur, unde localis motus cœli fit initium. Nam & animalia dextra parte semper plus ualent uiribus, dextra item pars in animalibus plus caloris obtinet, quo nimirum ad motum atque ad agitationem fit paratior. Fit autem motus cœlestis initium ab oriente: quandoquidem uidemus stellas quotidie ab oriente in occidentem rapi. Igitur in oriente dextra cœli pars appositè notatur. Porrò perspecta ratione unius partis, procliue est iudicare de omnibus partibus reliquis.
main_text.head: Utrum cœlum dividatur in plura corpora seu sphæras mobiles?
main_text.p: Libro 2. cap.3.Cœlum dividitur in plures partes, plura corpora siue sphæras, easdemq; circulariter circumactas: quod probatur μεθόδῳ συνθετικῇ [?], id est, compositiua, in qua à primo proceditur ad ultimum id de quo est quæstio.
1.Si cœlum est quoddam corpus diuinum perfeƈtissimum, necessum est motum quoq; eius sempiternum & circularem, ac plane perfectissimum existere. qua de re nonnulla ante dicta sunt.

page.notes: The first word of the page is partly hidden by the fold, so "oriente" is read from its visible letters. The Greek phrase in the second paragraph is hard to read at this scan resolution and is marked [?]. The printed "perfeƈtissimum" is read as "perfectissimum"; the long s is written as plain s throughout. The final word of the page is the catchword "Si". The note "Libro 2. cap.3." is printed as two short lines in the margin.
